incident-bot: 🚨 INCIDENT ALERT: Streaming API /v1/generate p99 latency spike detected. Service SLO breach (p95/99) starting 2026-03-15T14:12:xxZ. Automated paging to oncall.

Maya Patel: saw the alert, joining. p99 is ~2.8s (baseline ~350ms). Streaming stalls reported by a few customers (chunks stop 4-8s).

Raj Singh: adding immediate context — we rolled int8 calibration to canary yesterday night on model rl-instruct-13b-quant. Canary load ~10% of traffic. Telemetry shows tail increase aligned with the canary window.

Eli Gomez: logs look like repeated KV cache eviction spikes during long-context streams. Stack traces show dequant step taking longer than expected right after kv-pop. P95 also drifting.

Zoe Lin: customer-impact: Support reported two enterprise customers experienced 5+ second stalls and one timed-out request. CS gave low-level incident tickets.

SRE Oncall: immediate mitigation proposals: 1) Reroute traffic off the canary model to fallback fp16 variant 2) Pause new canary ramps 3) Enable emergency autoscale on dedicated pools. Which should we do now?

Maya Patel: do 1 + 2 now. Rolling fallback to fp16 reduces perf risk. Raj, can you push config?

Raj Singh: on it. Running rollback route policy: 
```bash
# route-switch to fallback model variant
redwoodctl route update --route streaming --from rl-instruct-13b-quant --to rl-instruct-13b-fp16 --mode gradual --step 30%
```
Applying now. Will monitor p50/p95/p99.

incident-bot: Route update queued at 2723456790, expected 30s to propagate.

Eli Gomez: while route flips, I'm starting a live profile of the quantized kernel on the canary host. Early traces show dequant path CPU stalls at ~60ms spikes coinciding with token flush. Suspect calibration tables causing heavier memory copies.

ML Infra: flagged — we pushed a calibration table change (reduce LUT compression) which could increase memory ops. That landed in canary image 02:14 UTC. Rolling back that change might help but it requires model reload.

Zoe Lin: CS: notifying affected customers with ETA: "we're routing your traffic to the safe fallback variant and monitoring. We'll provide follow-up after stabilizing."

SRE Oncall: route rollout at 30% -> 60% -> 100% completed 4m. p99 dropped from 2.8s -> 420ms within two steps. Streaming stalls count down 90%.

Raj Singh: confirming, full traffic is now on fp16 fallback. Canary quant instance being isolated for investigation. Leaving canary at 0% for now.

Eli Gomez: collecting kernel traces and memory metrics. Snapshotting quant-calib artifact for further offline profiling: `s3://redwood-prod-debug/2723456789/quant-snapshot.tgz`.

ML Infra: next steps — reproduce locally with calibration table A/B, try reverting LUT compression and re-run microbenchmarks. If repro, we'll prepare a patched calibration that keeps size but restores copy path.

Maya Patel: escalation: If we can't get safe calibration in 60m, we should consider blocking this calibration from auto-promote and add gating to rollout pipeline.

Support Lead: customer updates sent. No active escalations. One customer asked for SLA credit guidance; please loop sales if needed.

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated (routing fallback) — monitoring. Postmortem required: include calibration change diff, rollout timeline, and customer impact notes. Paging cleared for oncall after handoff.

Raj Singh: creating a follow-up ticket: INF-2723456789 — will include perf traces and proposed calibration patch.

Maya Patel: thanks team. Assigning owners: Raj -> rollback/repro, Eli -> kernel traces and perf fix, ML Infra -> calibration patch + rollout gating, Support Lead -> customer comms. Meet for 15m RC sync in #incidents post-mitigation.

Zoe Lin: closing loop — p99 stabilized under SLO after full fallback. Will start drafting postmortem template. :white_check_mark:
